answer: Each agent carries a hardware‑bound identity token signed with a post‑quantum cipher and periodically emits a signed pulse tied to a unique juniper‑seeded timing channel. Validators cross‑check the pulse against a public ledger; any duplicate or out‑of‑phase token triggers a quarantine flag that isolates the suspect node. An attacker must forge the cipher and synchronize thousands of pulses, costing computational resources exponential in the network size.
